comments.body:
## A live close failed on this today — f10f, 2026-11-02

This stopped being hypothetical. `f10f-c24a-3cfa-449e` carries a genuinely
non-codebase criterion (an operator applies Terraform and records a real
Bedrock call), written in natural markdown as:

```
- [ ] `[non-codebase]` An operator applies this Terraform and records an attestation ...
```

`rebar transition f10f-c24a-3cfa-449e in_progress closed` **failed with RC=1**
on that single item. The tag was present and correctly spelled; only the
backticks defeated it.

### Executable confirmation

Run against the live matcher in the repo checkout:

```python
from rebar.llm.plan_review.det_operator_attested import _OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE as R
```

| checkbox text | result |
| --- | --- |
| `- [ ] [non-codebase] An operator applies this Terraform.` | MATCH |
| ``- [ ] `[non-codebase]` An operator applies this Terraform.`` | **NOMATCH** |
| ``- [x] `[non-codebase]` An operator applies this Terraform.`` | **NOMATCH** |
| `- [ ] [operator-attested] An operator applies this.` | MATCH |
| ``- [ ] `[operator-attested]` An operator applies this.`` | **NOMATCH** |

Two findings beyond the title's claim:

1. **Both spellings** are defeated, not just the canonical one. The
   compatibility alias gives no escape.
2. The **ticked** backticked form is also a NOMATCH. That matters for the
   other direction of this bug: a reader who ticks a backticked
   `[non-codebase]` box to get past the precheck has not recorded an attested
   item — `ensure_attested_items_valid` never sees it, so the `provenance:`
   requirement is skipped silently. The item passes as an ordinary ticked box.
   So the backtick does not merely withhold an exemption; it converts an
   attested criterion into an unattested one while looking correct.

### Why the author writes the backticks

In `- [ ] [non-codebase] ...`, the bare tag sits directly beside the checkbox
and reads as a second empty bracket pair. Backticking it is what a careful
markdown author does to disambiguate, and it renders better everywhere the
description is displayed. The failure mode therefore selects against careful
authors.

### Note on the f10f resolution

f10f was not resolved by fixing this. The criterion was genuinely satisfied —
Terraform applied, before/after Bedrock calls recorded — so the box was ticked
on its merits. Per finding 2 above, that tick means the item is now treated as
an ordinary criterion rather than an attested one, which is the wrong shape for
what it is even though the outcome is correct.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

The `[non-codebase]` acceptance-criterion tag is silently inert when written in backticks at the start of the checkbox text, the ordinary markdown form and the one rebar's guidance rendered. The criterion looks exempt, reviews as exempt, and is refused at close. The close of `f10f-c24a-3cfa-449e` failed (RC=1) on 2026-11-02 on exactly this after its change merged.

The canonical matcher `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py:48-51`) requires the bare bracketed token right after the checkbox. Measured by importing it: the backticked form does not match for `- [ ]`, `- [x]`, or the `[operator-attested]` alias. Every deterministic parser of the tag imports it or its sibling `_TAG_AT_START_RE` (`:190-192`):

- Close precheck `ensure_ac_boxes_checked` (`src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:528`) refuses the item as unchecked.
- `ensure_attested_items_valid` (`txn.py:564`) relies on `laundering_gaps` (`det_attestation_launder.py:111`) and `provenance_gaps` (`det_measurement_provenance.py:136`), which skip the item, so a TICKED backticked box is handled as an ordinary criterion and its `provenance:` and laundering checks are skipped.
- `operator_evidence_ac_gaps` (`det_operator_attested.py:158`) and `misplaced_tag_lines` (`:196-205`) neither honour nor report it.
- `decide_ops.operator_attested_ac_texts` (`decide_ops.py:30-35`) omits it.
- The LLM prompts `completion_verifier.md:92-94` and `plan_review_evidence_kind.md:55-58` do not say whether a backticked tag counts.

## Approach

Widen the accepted surface (settled here: narrowing the guidance would leave descriptions already written that way broken). In `det_operator_attested.py`, define the tag form once as a non-capturing alternation of the bare token and the token wrapped in one balanced pair of backticks, and build both start-anchored patterns from it. This fits because every deterministic consumer imports from this one module, so one change makes all of them agree by construction; the non-capturing form keeps the single capture group that `decide_ops` `.findall()` needs. Both spellings share the alternation, so they cannot diverge. Unchanged: the tag counts only at the start of the checkbox text; a later mention (code span or not) is not a tag; unbalanced or doubled backticks are not accepted; matching stays exact and case-insensitive.

Then align the surfaces that describe the tag: both LLM prompts state the backticked form counts the same; the `txn.py` close-refusal message names the exact form `- [ ] [non-codebase] <criterion>` and says backticks are also accepted; `docs/plan-review-gate.md` records the backticked form. The evidence-kind prompt text is rendered into the generated `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` (regenerated with `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide`), and its tag-contract lines are digest-pinned in `tests/unit/test_measurement_provenance_criterion.py` `CONTRACT_DIGESTS`, which is a deliberate-update gate, so the pin is recomputed in this change. `completion_reconcile.py`, `det_advisory.py`, and `coach_moves.py` already show the bare form or mention the tag in prose, so they need no text change; a test proves their examples are accepted.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py` — shared tag form; both start patterns.
- `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py` — close-refusal message.
- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md`, `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_evidence_kind.md` — tag contract.
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md`; `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` (regenerated).
- `tests/unit/test_measurement_provenance_criterion.py` — recomputed digest pin.
- `tests/unit/test_non_codebase_backticked_tag.py` — new regression tests.

## Testing

New module `tests/unit/test_non_codebase_backticked_tag.py`, observed failing before the fix:

- Happy path: backticked and bare forms of both spellings under `- [ ]` and `- [x]` match with the same captured text.
- Close: an unchecked backticked item is exempt; an untagged unchecked item is still refused.
- Ticked backticked box: provenance and laundering gaps are reported and the close guard refuses it.
- DET checks: the operator-evidence lint, misplaced-tag lint, and `decide_ops` treat it as tagged.
- Edge: unbalanced backticks, a later code-span mention, a near-miss token, and an empty criterion do not match.
- Guidance: every tag example in the guidance surfaces matches.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Backticked and bare `[non-codebase]` capture the same criterion text under `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` for `- [ ]` and `- [x]`; verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_non_codebase_backticked_tag.py -k resolve_the_same`.
- [x] The `[operator-attested]` alias resolves identically in both forms; verified by the alias cases of `-k resolve_the_same` in that module.
- [x] `ensure_ac_boxes_checked` does not refuse an unchecked backticked-tag item; verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_non_codebase_backticked_tag.py -k exempt_from_the_close_precheck`.
- [x] A ticked backticked-tag box without provenance is refused by `ensure_attested_items_valid`; verified by `-k close_refuses_a_ticked_backticked` in that module.
- [x] `provenance_gaps` reports a ticked backticked-tag item lacking provenance; verified by `-k provenance_gap` in that module.
- [x] `laundering_gaps` reports a ticked backticked-tag item citing a test path; verified by `-k laundering` in that module.
- [x] `misplaced_tag_lines` does not report a backticked tag at the start; verified by `-k not_misplaced` in that module.
- [x] `operator_evidence_ac_gaps` treats a backticked-tag item as tagged; verified by `-k operator_evidence_lint` in that module.
- [x] `operator_attested_ac_texts` returns the criterion text of a backticked-tag item; verified by `-k decide_ops` in that module.
- [x] Unbalanced backticks, a later code-span mention, a near-miss token, and an empty criterion do not match; verified by `-k non_tags_stay_unmatched` in that module.
- [x] Every tag example in `completion_reconcile.py`, `det_operator_attested.py`, `txn.py`, and `writing-a-passing-plan.md` matches; verified by `-k every_guidance_example` in that module.
- [x] Each LLM prompt states the backticked tag counts the same; verified by `git grep -n backtick -- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_evidence_kind.md` showing a hit in each file.
- [x] The `txn.py` close-refusal message contains `- [ ] [non-codebase] <criterion>`; verified by `-k exact_form` in that module.
- [x] `make verify` passes in the worktree before push.
